newsitem.title: Australia: Australian debt eases slightly as RBA stays quiet.
newsitem.headline: Australian debt eases slightly as RBA stays quiet.

text.p: *Australian debt futures eased back slightly from their earlier highs as the Reserve Bank made no announcement on policy after Tuesday's board meeting.
Australian debt futures eased back slightly from their earlier highs as the Reserve Bank made no announcement on policy after Tuesday's board meeting.

The chances of the central bank easing again so soon after the last rate cut on May 23 had been seen as extremely slim, although the market was not prepared to take any chances after the shock timing of the move to 5.5 percent, and was reasonbly firm going into the RBA's 9.30 a.m. policy announcement time.
The market is now focused on first quarter GDP at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT). Median forecasts centre on a 0.8 percent rise after the 0.5 percent growth in the December quarter.

However, this would take the annual rate down to 2.2 percent from 3.1 percent due to a large March quarter 1996 rise being removed from the equation. "Something below the medium, say up 0.6 percent (on the quarter) will be taken as positive by the market," said one bond trader. "I think the risk is for the curve to flatten with the long-end now offering more value."
June three-year bond yield hit a 3-1/4 year low of around 6.10 percent in after hours trading on the outside chance of a rate cut and just 60 basis points over the current cash level.

Spread margins were fairly mixed against the dollar bloc with the long end slightly lagging a rally in U.S. Treasuries on Tuesday, where hopes remain for slowing growth in the second quarter. However, the market outperformed Canadian debt in the aftermath of Tuesday's Canadian election.
